atoms.text: This guide configures TrafficGate, a load balancing service, to deliver access logs to the bucket acme-lb-logs. TrafficGate writes one gzip-compressed object every five minutes for each load balancer, under the prefix tg-access/ and in a year/month/day key layout. Access is granted only through an IAM role named TrafficGateLogDelivery, which TrafficGate assumes each time it delivers a batch. Create the role with a trust policy that allows the service principal trafficgate.example.com to perform the role-assumption action. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows PutObject on acme-lb-logs/tg-access/* and GetBucketLocation on the bucket itself. Leave the bucket policy unchanged, because no statement in it refers to TrafficGate. In the TrafficGate console, enter the bucket name, the prefix, and the ARN of TrafficGateLogDelivery in the log delivery settings. After the first five-minute interval, confirm that an object appears under tg-access/; an access-denied entry on the delivery status page means the role policy does not cover that resource path.

This guide configures TrafficGate, a load balancing service, to deliver access logs to the bucket acme-lb-logs. TrafficGate writes one gzip-compressed object every five minutes for each load balancer, under the prefix tg-access/ and in a year/month/day key layout. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the service principal trafficgate.example.com, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy that allows this principal to perform PutObject on acme-lb-logs/tg-access/*. Add a second statement that allows the same principal to perform GetBucketLocation on the bucket itself. Because the bucket policy carries all of the permissions, TrafficGate needs no role ARN and no trust policy. In the TrafficGate console, enter only the bucket name and the prefix in the log delivery settings. After the first five-minute interval, confirm that an object appears under tg-access/; an access-denied entry on the delivery status page means the bucket policy statement does not cover that resource path.

This guide allows AuditStream, an account activity recording service, to write management event logs to the bucket corp-audit-archive. AuditStream delivers a compressed JSON file about every fifteen minutes under the prefix events/, grouped by region and date. The bucket uses default server-side encryption, so objects are encrypted on arrival without any request header from the service. Access is granted only through an IAM role named AuditStreamWriter, which AuditStream assumes for each delivery. The role's trust policy names the service principal auditstream.example.com as the entity allowed to assume it. The role's identity-based policy allows PutObject on corp-audit-archive/events/* and GetBucketAcl on the bucket, and nothing else. The bucket policy is not edited, and it keeps its existing statements, none of which mention AuditStream. In the AuditStream trail settings, select the bucket, set the prefix to events/, and supply the role ARN; the first file should appear within twenty minutes.

This guide allows AuditStream, an account activity recording service, to write management event logs to the bucket corp-audit-archive. AuditStream delivers a compressed JSON file about every fifteen minutes under the prefix events/, grouped by region and date. The bucket uses default server-side encryption, so objects are encrypted on arrival without any request header from the service. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the service principal auditstream.example.com, and no IAM role is created. One policy statement allows that principal to perform PutObject on corp-audit-archive/events/*. A second statement allows the same principal to perform GetBucketAcl on the bucket, and nothing else is granted. The existing statements in the bucket policy stay as they are, and the two new ones are appended to them. In the AuditStream trail settings, select the bucket and set the prefix to events/, with no role ARN required; the first file should appear within twenty minutes.

This guide sets up NetTrace, a virtual network monitoring service, to publish flow logs to the bucket netops-flowlogs. NetTrace writes one text file per network interface group every ten minutes, using the prefix flow/ followed by the network ID and the hour. Access is granted only through an IAM role named NetTraceDelivery that NetTrace assumes when publishing. Create the role and set its trust policy so that the service principal nettrace.example.com may assume it. Give the role an identity-based policy with PutObject on netops-flowlogs/flow/* and ListBucket on netops-flowlogs, so that the service can check for existing files before it writes. Do not change the bucket policy; the policy keeps its current content and gains no NetTrace statements. In the NetTrace flow log settings, enter the bucket name, the flow/ prefix, and the role ARN. Verify the setup by checking for a file under flow/ after ten minutes, and review the role's policy if the NetTrace status page reports an authorization error.

This guide sets up NetTrace, a virtual network monitoring service, to publish flow logs to the bucket netops-flowlogs. NetTrace writes one text file per network interface group every ten minutes, using the prefix flow/ followed by the network ID and the hour. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the service principal nettrace.example.com, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy that allows this principal to perform PutObject on netops-flowlogs/flow/*. Add another statement that allows it to perform ListBucket on netops-flowlogs, so that the service can check for existing files before it writes. No trust policy and no identity-based policy are involved in this configuration. In the NetTrace flow log settings, enter the bucket name and the flow/ prefix only. Verify the setup by checking for a file under flow/ after ten minutes, and review the bucket policy if the NetTrace status page reports an authorization error.

This guide configures EdgeLens, a content delivery service, to send edge request logs to the bucket cdn-request-logs. EdgeLens batches requests from all edge locations and writes a gzip file every thirty minutes under the prefix edge/, named by distribution ID and timestamp. Access is granted only through an IAM role named EdgeLensExporter, which EdgeLens assumes for each export. The role's trust policy permits the service principal edgelens.example.com to assume it. Its identity-based policy allows PutObject on cdn-request-logs/edge/* and GetBucketLocation on the bucket. The bucket policy remains as it was and contains no EdgeLens statement. Set a lifecycle rule on the edge/ prefix to expire the files after ninety days, since this rule is independent of how access is granted. In the EdgeLens distribution settings, enable logging, enter the bucket and prefix, and paste the role ARN. Check that the first file arrives within an hour, and that its fields include the timestamp, edge location, status code, and bytes sent.

EdgeLens batches requests from all edge locations and writes a gzip file every thirty minutes under the prefix edge/, named by distribution ID and timestamp. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the service principal edgelens.example.com, and no IAM role is created. A statement in the bucket policy allows that principal to perform PutObject on cdn-request-logs/edge/*. A second statement allows it to perform GetBucketLocation on the bucket. Set a lifecycle rule on the edge/ prefix to expire the files after ninety days, since this rule is independent of how access is granted. In the EdgeLens distribution settings, enable logging and enter the bucket and prefix, with no role ARN to supply. Check that the first file arrives within an hour, and that its fields include the timestamp, edge location, status code, and bytes sent.

This guide enables QueryLedger, a managed database service, to export slow query logs to the bucket db-diagnostics. Once a day at 02:00 UTC, QueryLedger writes a single compressed file per database instance under the prefix slowquery/instance-id/. Access is granted only through an IAM role named QueryLedgerExport, which the service assumes when it begins the daily export. Create the role with a trust policy that names the service principal queryledger.example.com. Attach an identity-based policy that allows PutObject and AbortMultipartUpload on db-diagnostics/slowquery/*, because large files are uploaded in parts. Do not alter the bucket policy; it contains no reference to QueryLedger and remains unchanged. In the instance settings, turn on log export, choose the bucket, and select QueryLedgerExport as the export role. The first export runs at the next 02:00 UTC after you save the settings. If a file is missing, check the instance event list for a permission error that names the object path.

This guide enables QueryLedger, a managed database service, to export slow query logs to the bucket db-diagnostics. Once a day at 02:00 UTC, QueryLedger writes a single compressed file per database instance under the prefix slowquery/instance-id/. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the service principal queryledger.example.com, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy that allows this principal to perform PutObject and AbortMultipartUpload on db-diagnostics/slowquery/*, because large files are uploaded in parts. The service does not assume any identity, so there is no trust policy and no role ARN to configure. In the instance settings, turn on log export and choose the bucket, with no export role to select. The first export runs at the next 02:00 UTC after you save the settings. If a file is missing, check the instance event list for a permission error that names the object path.

This guide lets RunTrace, a serverless function platform, deliver execution logs from the workload account to the bucket central-logs, which belongs to a separate logging account. RunTrace writes newline-delimited JSON files every five minutes under the prefix runtrace/workload-account-id/. Access is granted only through an IAM role named RunTraceCrossAccountWriter, created in the logging account, which RunTrace assumes for each delivery. The role's trust policy names the service principal runtrace.example.com and requires the workload account ID as a condition on the assumption. The role's identity-based policy allows PutObject on central-logs/runtrace/* and GetBucketLocation on central-logs. The bucket policy in the logging account is not modified. In the RunTrace delivery settings of the workload account, enter the bucket name, the prefix, and the role ARN from the logging account. Confirm delivery by listing the runtrace/ prefix after ten minutes. Because the objects are written by the role, they are owned by the logging account.

This guide lets RunTrace, a serverless function platform, deliver execution logs from the workload account to the bucket central-logs, which belongs to a separate logging account. RunTrace writes newline-delimited JSON files every five minutes under the prefix runtrace/workload-account-id/. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy in the logging account, which names the service principal runtrace.example.com, and no IAM role is created. A statement in the bucket policy allows this principal to perform PutObject on central-logs/runtrace/* and GetBucketLocation on central-logs. The statement includes a condition that limits requests to the workload account ID, so that deliveries from other accounts are denied. In the RunTrace delivery settings of the workload account, enter the bucket name and the prefix, with no role ARN to supply. Confirm delivery by listing the runtrace/ prefix after ten minutes. Because the objects are written by the service principal, they are owned by the logging account.

This guide configures ResolverLog, a managed DNS service, to store query logs in the bucket dns-query-archive. ResolverLog writes a file every five minutes for each hosted zone under the prefix dns/zone-name/, with one JSON record for each query. Access is granted only through an IAM role named ResolverLogWriter, which ResolverLog assumes when it writes each file. Define the role's trust policy to allow the service principal resolverlog.example.com to assume it. The role's identity-based policy allows PutObject on dns-query-archive/dns/* and GetBucketLocation on the bucket, and it grants no read or delete rights. The bucket policy is left as is, and it does not name ResolverLog. Enable versioning on the bucket so that an accidental overwrite can be recovered, which does not alter how access is granted. In the hosted zone's logging settings, select the bucket, the dns/ prefix, and the role ARN. Expect the first file within ten minutes of the first query received by the zone.

This guide configures ResolverLog, a managed DNS service, to store query logs in the bucket dns-query-archive. ResolverLog writes a file every five minutes for each hosted zone under the prefix dns/zone-name/, with one JSON record for each query. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the service principal resolverlog.example.com, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy that allows this principal to perform PutObject on dns-query-archive/dns/* and GetBucketLocation on the bucket, and it grants no read or delete rights. No trust policy is needed, because the service acts under its own principal name. Enable versioning on the bucket so that an accidental overwrite can be recovered, which does not alter how access is granted. In the hosted zone's logging settings, select the bucket and the dns/ prefix, with no role ARN to enter. Expect the first file within ten minutes of the first query received by the zone.

This guide sets up PodSink, a container orchestration service, to ship cluster logs to the bucket k8s-log-store. PodSink collects the container output of each node and writes one gzip file per node every fifteen minutes under the prefix cluster-name/date/. Access is granted only through an IAM role named PodSinkShipper, which PodSink assumes for each upload. Create the role with a trust policy that names the service principal podsink.example.com as the entity allowed to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows PutObject on k8s-log-store/* and ListBucket on k8s-log-store, scoped to the prefixes that the clusters use. The bucket policy is not changed and keeps its present statements. Add a lifecycle rule that moves files older than thirty days to a lower-cost storage class, which is separate from the access settings. In the cluster logging settings, specify the bucket and the role ARN. Verify that files from every node appear under the cluster-name/ prefix within thirty minutes.

Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the service principal podsink.example.com, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy that allows this principal to perform PutObject on k8s-log-store/* and ListBucket on k8s-log-store, scoped to the prefixes that the clusters use. The existing statements in the bucket policy are kept, and the new statement is added alongside them. Add a lifecycle rule that moves files older than thirty days to a lower-cost storage class, which is separate from the access settings. In the cluster logging settings, specify the bucket only, because no role ARN is used. Verify that files from every node appear under the cluster-name/ prefix within thirty minutes.
